Significant Cyber Incidents, 2003-2026

  • A spate of cyber attacks has rocked Japan – and it's spooked lawmakers
    10-23 10:30 EST

    A wave of cyber attacks has disrupted more than 20 Japanese companies across transport, retail, finance and cloud services. Rail operator JR East reported losing 1.67 million email addresses, Times Car lost a large number of customer driving licence scans, cloud provider IDC Frontier reported a ransomware attack, and nine banks were reportedly hacked using AI. In response, Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party has called on the government to set up a cybersecurity task force to strengthen defences against AI-driven threats, after the head of its cybersecurity headquarters declared "a state of emergency in cyber space." Research by Macnica counted 119 attacks in Japan this year as of 6 October, up from 86 in 2025.

  • More Ontario police forces pause Crime Stoppers use after cyber breach
    10-23 10:05 EST

    Police forces in Halton, Peel and York regions, Hamilton and Kingston have suspended their use of Crime Stoppers. This follows Toronto Crime Stoppers pausing its phone, online and app-based tip intake over a cybersecurity breach that may have exposed identifying information in some anonymous tips. In March, hackers stole data from P3, the tip-management platform run by Navigate360. Toronto Crime Stoppers says the provider first told it that Toronto submissions weren't affected. It later learned that 176,859 tips submitted between January 2022 and November 2025 were affected, and 12,392 of them may contain personal information.

  • Fisher & Paykel breach puts cyber cover gaps on broker agenda
    10-23 09:49 EST

    Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, the NZX-listed medical device maker, said unauthorised parties accessed some company files and two employee email accounts, and some of those files contained personally identifiable information. The company is notifying the people affected and has told the relevant authorities. It said there is no evidence its patient data system was compromised and no impact on its products, manufacturing or supply chain. It believes the incident is contained, with no sign of ransomware or malware, and expects no material financial impact, though its shares fell as much as 1.5% after the disclosure.

  • Alabama Resumes Online Nurse Licensing After Cyber Incident
    10-22 13:19 EST

    The Alabama Board of Nursing switched to paper applications after a ransomware attack in August. Six weeks later, it has brought registered nurse license renewals back online in a new system, and initial exam applications are expected to return next. Investigators found that data was collected and downloaded during the attack, though containment measures kept the breach from escalating. The data that may have been exposed includes names, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, professional licensing information and medical information. The board oversees more than 97,000 licensed nurses. About 60,000 nurses with single-state licenses still have to renew by the Dec. 1 deadline, which has not been extended, and the investigation is ongoing.

  • Laboratory operator Quest reports cyber breach affecting patient records
    10-22 11:35 EST

    Quest Diagnostics said that on Wednesday it learned of unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system, which some clients use to place test orders and get results. The company believes an unauthorized party accessed certain patient records, but the full scope is still under investigation. Quest has notified federal law enforcement and started its incident response procedures, and it says the incident has not materially disrupted its business operations, though its shares fell 3.7% in premarket trading.

  • Hacking attempts surge as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
    10-22 00:08 EST

    Companies and governments around the world rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the internet. Cloud firms reported a surge in hacking attempts, with Cloudflare saying exploitation attempts climbed from thousands before the flaws were announced to millions afterward, and Amazon also reported widespread exploitation. Banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki were shut down as emergency measures, including services at Nomura, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, ANA, East Japan Railway, Asahi, Tokio Marine and Japan's Ministry of Finance.

  • MSU Federal Credit Union website goes dark amid cyber vulnerability
    10-21 15:57 EST

    On Wednesday, Oct. 21, the MSU Federal Credit Union in Lansing, Michigan, was one of many organizations whose websites went down temporarily after the FBI warned about a possible vulnerability, which the PHP Foundation has since released fixes for. The NSA also advised organizations to take systems offline if they couldn't update right away. MSUFCU said it took its website and digital banking offline "out of an abundance of caution" while it updates its systems and adds security measures. It said it doesn't believe any member information was compromised, and debit and credit cards still work.
